items.title: A real Settings window
items.text: ⌘, (Preferences…) now opens a Settings window laid out like System Settings: Appearance with a live preview and a light/dark theme picker, Panes & Windows, Terminal, Keyboard, Sessions & Agent, Remote Machines, Updates, and every other option under Advanced. Search finds any setting. Each row explains itself, marks what you've changed, and can reset to the default.

items.title: Your config file stays yours
items.text: Each change edits just that one line of your config file, keeping your comments and layout. Ghoztty checks the value before writing it, applies it right away, and backs the file up first. Open Config File… is still one click away.

items.title: New options
items.text: Choose the window gradient, how the pane sidebar starts (remember, expanded, collapsed or hidden), the smallest a pane can get before panes stack, and how much room hero mode's carousel takes.

items.title: Shortcut guide
items.text: Press ⌘/ (or Help → Keyboard Shortcuts, or the command palette) to see every shortcut you have, including the ones you changed, grouped and named in plain language. Search by name or by keys, click a shortcut to run it, or print a cheat sheet.

items.title: All windows by default
items.text: The sidebar opens showing all windows, and remembers if you switch to just this window.

items.title: Steadier edge drags
items.text: Dragging the sidebar's edge no longer makes the card or a tucking strip flicker.
